critical_code_review_comments: ReceiptResult.jsx correctly pre-builds a PNG blob and exposes a real <a href=blob:... download=...png> so the user's tap is the actual save gesture — this is the correct fix for the mobile/preview-iframe programmatic click() suppression.

URL.revokeObjectURL is called only on unmount cleanup; if items change during the same mount the previous objUrl is not revoked (minor memory leak). Consider revoking the previous URL when a new one is generated.
Two DialogContent instances in the codebase warn: 'Missing Description or aria-describedby={undefined}' — a11y-only warning, not blocking.

rca of the issue: Original bug: previous code called saveReceiptImage() which built the canvas after async awaits then invoked link.click() programmatically. The user-activation token was consumed by the button click before the async work, so by the time the synthetic click fired, the browser (esp. Safari + sandboxed preview iframes) silently no-op'd the download while a success toast still ran. Fix (verified): ReceiptResult.jsx pre-computes the blob into an object URL as soon as the receipt mounts, then exposes a real that the USER taps directly — a genuine gesture that always downloads. Additionally it renders the PNG in an for iOS 'long-press → Save Image' and a Web Share button for native gallery save. No more standalone 'Gambar tersimpan' toast.
